subject: Post-call recap: Acme Corp - TCO & token economics follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Acme Corp - TCO & token economics follow-up

Thanks for taking the time today, John. Quick recap from our call + next steps so your team can share with procurement.

Key pain points you called out:
- High per-interaction cost for your current setup (mainly due to lack of batching + redundant model hot-paths).
- Latency spikes during peak hours impacting UX (search-rewrite & assistant flows).
- Audit/compliance needs for usage logs and retention for regulated customers.

Goals we heard:
- Reduce per-response inference costs by ~40% without increasing median latency >20ms.
- Maintain or improve accuracy for the assistant use cases (few-shot prompts + KV cache).
- Get a predictable monthly invoice for budgeting and procurement.

High-level TCO levers we discussed (see attached ACME_TCO_v1.xlsx for line-item math):
1) Model choice + quantization: moving from FP16 to int8-ready variants for batchable workloads reduces runtime GPU memory and cost; estimated 15-25% cost improvement for heavy sampling scenarios.
2) Batching & workload-aware autoscaling: continuous batching for short responses + request shaping estimated to cut per-token cost by 20-35%.
3) Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (search + personalization): up to 50% token savings on tail queries.
4) Reserved Dedicated capacity vs. Hosted: for steady-state volume (your estimate: ~100M tokens/mo), Reserved capacity can provide 25-40% unit-cost savings versus purely on-demand hosted pricing.

Example back-of-envelope (numbers in attached sheet):
- Estimated monthly tokens (median case): 100M tokens
- Hosted list pricing baseline: $0.06 / 1k tokens => ~$6,000
- With batching + caching + quantization applied: estimated net cost ~$2,500-3,500 / mo (40-60% reduction)
- Dedicated reserved pricing (committed): estimated $1,800-3,700 / mo for equivalent throughput (depends on burst profile & SLA)

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll share the TCO workbook (attached) and a short pricing estimate PDF.
2) Ben (cc'd) can run a quick perf estimate and confirm latency SLOs for the suggested configuration.
3) If numbers look good, we can set up a short procurement-friendly packet (SOW + security evidence).

Ask: can you confirm the monthly active users & typical tokens per session so we lock numbers in? Emily from procurement — looping you in for timeline visibility.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Acme Corp - TCO & token economics follow-up

Marissa, thanks for the clear recap and the workbook. Quick answers from our side:
- Monthly MAUs for the assistant: ~40k (heavy enterprise users)
- Avg tokens per session (response side): ~200 tokens
- Peak concurrency: roughly 120 qps over a 30-minute window during business hours

Budget constraints: procurement gave a rough target of $3k-$3.5k/month for inference (we might be able to stretch for a clear ROI case). Key procurement asks: line-item pricing, audit logs, and a clear migration path with an SLA.

A couple of clarifying questions from my engineering lead:
1) How conservative are your batching savings estimates for interactive sessions (50-100ms client latency target)?
2) Can you provide an MLP for KV cache hit ratios — what assumptions did you use to get to 50% token savings?

If the numbers line up we can present to procurement next Wednesday (4/15).

John, great context, thanks. Short answers inline: 

1) Batching savings & latency impact:
- For interactive flows we size batches aggressively for short tails: continuous batching incurs ~5-15ms extra server-side queuing for targets under 200ms end-to-end; that matches many customers' SLAs. The 20-35% number in the sheet assumes median response lengths (150-250 tokens) and a mixed read/write profile. For ultra-low latency (<50ms) use cases the gains are smaller.

2) KV cache assumptions:
- We modeled cache hit rates based on three buckets: cold (no cache) 40% of requests, warm (simple personalization/prefix reuse) 45% — hit rate 30-40%, hot (templates / repeated queries) 15% — hit rate 80-90%. Weighted average token reduction = ~48% in our sample. We can replace these with your telemetry for a custom projection.

I've attached an updated redwood_pricing_estimate.pdf with both hosted and dedicated scenarios and a shaded section that maps to your $3k-$3.5k target. Short summary:
- If your profile is closer to the median case above, Hosted with caching + quantization fits within $3-4k/mo.
- If you want tighter latency with SLA and predictable unit cost, Dedicated reserved capacity brings it closer to $2-3k/mo with a 12-month commit.

Next steps I suggest:
- Ben will do a performance readout (short doc) that we can include in the procurement packet.
- If procurement wants pricing in a single-sheet SOW + draft contract, I can kick that off once you confirm willingness to move forward with a 12-month reserved option.

Can Ben and I target Tuesday to get the perf doc over to you? Also copying Emily so procurement can advise preferred contract format.

Thanks,
Marissa

John — Ben from SE here. Quick note on the perf/latency side and what I'll include in the perf doc:
- Test plan: we'll replay a 48-hour sample of your traffic (anonymized) against a dedicated config that uses int8 quantized model + 2-level KV cache + continuous batching.
- Metrics I'll provide: median/95th latency, qps-to-cost curve, and cache hit sensitivity (showing savings at 30/40/50% hit).
- Conservative estimate for your 120 qps peak: median latency target <220ms, 95th <400ms for the recommended config. We can tune for lower median at some additional cost.

I'll attach the perf doc + a draft SOW (SOW-draft-ACME.docx) and add line-item pricing. If you want, we can also schedule a short procurement/engineering call after you review the perf doc (15-20 minutes).

I'll get the artifacts to you by EOD Tuesday.

Cheers,
Ben
